ca_bonus_booty_boulder.blurb: Bonus Booty Boulder is a small boulder within the Treasure Cove bouldering area near Castle Peak, in the Donner and Truckee part of the I-80 corridor, at roughly 7,500 feet. It has seven problems running from VB up to V4, so most of what is here is on the gentler side, with two V4s at the top end. The boulder stands right beside the trail, about 50 yards downhill beyond the larger Treasure Chest Boulder. Mosquitoes can be thick in the cove, which is worth planning around.

ca_doom_wall.blurb: Doom Wall is a compact sport crag on the Central Coast, one of nine areas in the Silly Rock zone just off Highway 166 near the San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara county line. Seven bolted routes climb conglomerate, starting around 5.8 with a single 5.12 at the top, though the bulk of them sit in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. The wall sits in a small canyon where a breeze funnels through, which keeps it tolerable on warm days. The walk in from the roadside turnout is only a couple of minutes.

ca_b_frolic_towers.blurb: Frolic Towers is a pair of small formations in the Stirrup Tank area of Joshua Tree National Park's Pinto Basin, part of the larger Stirrup Towers group. One tower stands behind Star Trek Tower and the other stands close beside it. The seven routes are mostly traditional, with one bolted sport line and one top-rope, all on monzogranite. Grades span 5.8 to 5.10, and four of them are 5.8, which suits moderate leaders. The climbs face west, and the walk from the neighbouring tower takes only a few minutes.

ca_d_the_stirrup.blurb: The Stirrup is the large block capping the far end of the Stirrup Towers group in the Pinto Basin of Joshua Tree National Park, attached to Pyramid Tower. Its seven routes start on several sides of the block as well as at its base. Six are traditional and one is a top-rope, on monzogranite. Most grades fall between 5.6 and 5.9, with the top-rope line at 5.10. A couple of the routes carry serious-fall warnings, so it rewards confident gear placement. The approach is five minutes or less.

ca_hon_yak.blurb: Hon Yak is a crag in the Rock Creek canyon of the Eastern Sierra near Mammoth Lakes, at about 9,100 feet and visible from the road. It has seven routes, five trad and two sport, from 5.9 to 5.11, with most split between 5.10 and 5.11. The original lines were cleaned and given new anchors in 2017, and top-rope setups are possible from the anchors above. One 70 m rope handles every climb. Expect about a 15-minute walk up along the creek from the roadside pullout.

ca_bowling_ball_the.blurb: The Bowling Ball is a separate limestone formation near the main Marble Caves wall in northwest California, perched on a ridge above the South Fork of the Trinity River at about 4,000 feet. It has seven routes, five sport and two trad. Four fall in the 5.10 range, with one each at 5.11, 5.12 and 5.13. The stone is streaked in several colours. It can be seen from the main crag along the ridgeline.
ca_bowling_ball_the.approach: From the roadside pullout, follow the climbers' trail steeply downhill for about five minutes to the base of the formation.
ca_bowling_ball_the.parking_note: Continue along the main road past the pasture instead of turning for the main Marble Caves wall, and use the small pullout at mile post 10, usually marked by a cairn.

ca_conference_boulder.blurb: Conference Boulder is a single boulder in The Beach section of the Tramway bouldering zone, in Shangri-La Valley of the San Jacinto Mountains at about 8,400 feet. It has seven problems from V0 to V8, with the majority in the V5 to V8 range, plus a harder project. It sits near the edge of the mountain with views toward Palm Springs and Joshua Tree, roughly 100 feet from the Conspiracy boulder. Heavy lichen and debris cover some of the lines, so expect to clean before climbing.
